headers.comment: Applied to every response. script-src is strict and has no unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, which is the directive that actually prevents XSS. style-src needs unsafe-inline because the generated markup carries 1,259 inline style attributes for layout; removing that would mean refactoring the whole build, so it is a recorded compromise rather than an oversight. connect-src allows exactly one outside origin, api.emailjs.com, because the contact form sends through EmailJS directly from the browser; the analytics beacon stays first-party.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.emailjs.com; media-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests
geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()

headers.comment: The dashboard is authenticated, must never be indexed, and must never be cached by anything in the middle.
API responses are never cached. The endpoints set their own headers too, belt and braces.
Pages revalidate. Content changes with every deploy and the HTML is small, so staleness costs more than the request does.
Filenames are not content-hashed, so assets get a moderate window with stale-while-revalidate rather than an immutable year. A one-day window means a deploy is picked up the same day without a purge.
